itemListElement.name: Discovery and Priorities
itemListElement.description: Clarify the main problem, relevant users and desired result. Record which facts are confirmed, which assumptions need testing and what an acceptable next step looks like. This avoids treating every problem as a request for more SEO, posts or software features.

itemListElement.name: Scope, Owners and Acceptance Criteria
itemListElement.description: Define deliverables, responsibilities, dependencies and the person authorized to approve each stage. Separate a website build from ongoing marketing, and separate a new software feature from an existing system capability. Timeline and commercial commitments are confirmed in the project agreement, not assumed from a generic page.

itemListElement.name: Research and Source Verification
itemListElement.description: Review the relevant audience journey, website condition, search intent or operational process. For public healthcare information, identify who owns the underlying facts and which claims need qualified clinical review. Platform and professional rules are checked against the actual content and campaign proposed.

itemListElement.name: Create, Build and Hand Off
itemListElement.description: Assign work to the relevant search, content or engineering specialist. A common website sequence is SEO page brief → content draft → content review → development implementation. A different scope may require design, software requirements or another approved workflow; no team member automatically signs off for another discipline.

itemListElement.name: Review, Revise and Approve
itemListElement.description: Reviewers comment on a specific draft or implementation. Changes return to the responsible owner with a clear request, updated version and review decision. A content correction is not the same as a new feature request; material scope changes are discussed before additional work is treated as approved.

itemListElement.name: Test and Release
itemListElement.description: Check the deliverable against agreed requirements. For a website, that may include mobile layout, working links, contact paths, approved facts and technical search controls. For software, it may include roles, access permissions, workflows and agreed user tests. Launch follows the required client and specialist approvals.

itemListElement.name: Report and Improve
itemListElement.description: Share evidence appropriate to the work: approved content, completed website tests, implemented functionality, search observations or responsibly defined campaign signals. Report the period and limitations; activity should not be presented as guaranteed patient results. Agree further improvements as a new task or next phase.
